newsitem.title: USA: USA Waste to buy United Waste, stocks tumble.
newsitem.headline: USA Waste to buy United Waste, stocks tumble.

text.p: The fast-paced consolidation among trash firms picked up more steam Monday as USA Waste Services Inc. said it would buy United Waste Systems Inc. in a stock deal valued at $1.7 billion.
But the stocks of both companies fell sharply due to views Houston-based USA Waste did not offer a rich-enough price and might be growing too fast.
Under the definitive agreement, USA Waste will offer 1.075 shares of its common stock for each United Waste share in a tax-free pooling of interests, the companies said in a joint statement.
United Waste's stock fell $4.25 to close at $33.375 on Nasdaq. USA Waste slid $3.375 to $31.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Based on the transaction ratio and Monday's stock decline, the deal valued United Waste shares at $34.27 each -- well below the stock's 52-week high of $41.75 reached last week.
"It's disappointing," said one trader.
"USA Waste is down because the United Waste price was not the big premium people were speculating about. They were looking for someting in the $40s," said an arbitrager who declined to be identified.
USA Waste acknowledged that Wall Street needed some convincing.

"What we need to do is get out there and talk to people about the transaction and why we're so pleased with it and why it will be accretive and the plans we have to make it a very good deal for both shareholder groups. Apparently it's not as well understood as we think it should be," said Lew Nevins, vice president for investor relations at USA Waste.

The solid waste industry is consolidating at a blistering rate as independent operators sell their assets to larger companies like United Waste which, in turn, are getting scooped up by a handful of giant players.

In a smaller transaction also announced Monday, Superior Services Inc. said it would buy some solid waste businesses from Browning-Ferris Industries Inc. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but Superior Services estimated revenues of the businesses at about $33 million.
The proposed United Waste transaction will be another significant step for acquisition-hungry USA Waste, the third-largest solid waste company in North America.

It recently completed a $518 million acquisition of the Canadian assets of Allied Waste Industries Inc., set a deal to buy Canadian assets of WMX Technologies Inc. for $186 million and last year bought Sanifill Inc. for $1.6 billion.

After the proposed United Waste deal, USA Waste will have annual revenues of about $2.1 billion and assets of more than $4.5 billion, they said. The combined company will operate 155 landfills, 270 collection companies and 153 transfer stations serving over 3 million customers in 42 states, Washington, D.C., Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico.

"We anticipate significant synergies and enhanced growth opportunities to result from this merger, which we expect will be accretive to our earnings," John Drury, chairman and chief executive of USA Waste, said in a news release.
USA Waste anticipates $29 million in savings and efficiencies from the combination, said Nevins.
He also said the transaction is expected to add at least 5 cents per share to USA Waste's earnings in its first year.
Although there is some geographic overlap between the two companies, USA Waste operates primarily in urban areas, while United Waste focuses on secondary, rural markets.
The deal is expected to close during the third quarter, subject to approval by the stockholders of the companies and regulators.
United Waste, the sixth-largest solid waste company in North America, will designate two people to the board of USA Waste.
USA Waste serves over 2 million municipal, commercial, industrial and residential customers in 36 states with 119 landfills, 203 collection companies and 80 transfer stations.
United Waste owns or operates 36 landfills, 67 collection companies and 73 transfer stations, serving more than 850,000 customers in 21 states.
